gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the same theorem-level error: a liminf result from a subgradient method is incorrectly strengthened to monotone convergence of the raw objective sequence. It also distinguishes the valid monotone convergence of the running minimum and supplies the corresponding repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both the gold issue and ISSUE-001 diagnose the unsupported claim that kappa(cDo(d_k)) itself decreases monotonically to kappa_*, despite the proof establishing only a liminf guarantee and the method not generally being a descent method; the monotone conclusion applies only to the running best values.

component_coverage.gold_component: The theorem falsely claims that the raw objective sequence kappa(cDo(d_k)) is monotone and converges to kappa_*; only its liminf is established, while the running best values are the valid monotone sequence.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that the cited framework yields only liminf-type convergence, that the raw iterates need not decrease because the method is not generally a descent method, and that only the running minimum is guaranteed to decrease to kappa_*. Its proposed deletion or replacement directly corrects the gold defect.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 identifies the same corollary error: under A_i=R_i^T R_i, using B_i=R_i^{-T} does not produce the claimed optimal scaling. It shows the mismatch between BB^T and A_i^{-1}, gives a strict suboptimality example, and supplies the corrected orientation B_i=R_i^{-1}.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both the gold issue and ISSUE-004 diagnose the wrong triangular Cholesky orientation in the partial-Cholesky right factor. R_i^{-T} yields a scaling based on (R_i R_i^T)^{-1}, not A_i^{-1}=(R_i^T R_i)^{-1}, so the claimed omega-optimality and eigenvalue argument fail; R_i^{-1} is the required correction.

component_coverage.gold_component: The proposed partial-Cholesky factor B_i=R_i^{-T} is not generally omega-optimal under A_i=R_i^T R_i because it gives the wrong BB^T orientation and can be strictly suboptimal.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly compares the products induced by R_i^{-T} with the required A_i^{-1}, demonstrates different spectra and a strictly worse omega value, explains why the displayed identity does not support the claim, and repairs the formula by replacing R_i^{-T} with R_i^{-1}.
